shoal_e22_entry.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_entry.text: On Day Four Hundred Nine, the association put three accepted mine-road scopes on the ordinary receiving table. Yue had finished her port wages and current reassessment before this new decision. No previous appointment supplied a hidden mandate to carry a different institution's property or direct strangers toward a job. Each proposed road would begin with actual port preparation, departure on Four Hundred Twenty-Five, and fifteen ordinary travel days before arrival at the mine on Four Hundred Forty.

shoal_e22_open_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_open_02.text: The current road carrier quoted twenty-four copper for its accepted shared carriage or ticket scope. It did not include personal meals and overnight costs. Yue had priced fifteen road living days at two copper each and would pay thirty from her own settled money. Her earlier twenty-copper planned reserve was increased by ten before booking. The current port room and meals remained paid through the accepted departure date, with no refund assumed for unused hours.

shoal_e22_open_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_open_03.text: Her own conservative purse could support that road. One hundred fourteen carried from settled Lark work, three hundred eighty earned from three completed port jobs, and two from the performed art task made four hundred ninety-six before conditional dispatch pay. Four hundred six covered personal room and meals after the arrival grant, eight actual clinic fees had been repaid eight through restitution, and extras stayed within sixteen. Thirty road living left at least forty-four after arrival.

shoal_e22_open_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_open_04.text: Conditional Lark dispatch pay added six only where the actual carried task had been completed. The arrival grant's sixteen lodging copper had paid the keeper directly and was not counted as personal cash. Institution care, materials, readers, and survey instruments also stayed outside her purse. Yue could read a funded role without depending on an invented balance. She could afford the ordinary road while still treating a new agreement as work, with costs beyond money.

shoal_e22_open_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_open_05.text: The cargo scope belonged to the port's current freight inventory. Six numbered crates of signal plates had remained outside the burned stores in a separate secured gallery. Their owners offered an ordinary escort and two receiving workdays at the mine, with defined supplier-bench access for the current freight comparison. The plates were no personal gift. Their presence would open a technical source and make the road's timetable answer to a cargo owner.

shoal_e22_open_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_open_06.text: The worker-journey scope concerned five consenting adults besides Yue. They were not a rescued family required to follow the association. Each had chosen to explore a different town without a promised job there. The source offered booked tickets, four arrival days' room and meals, and a narrow optional statement opportunity. It offered no supplier kit or bench. People's own changes of mind would be part of the road rather than defects in freight receiving.

shoal_e22_open_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_open_07.text: The independent survey scope belonged to the Outer Shoal Pilots' Association. It offered an unpowered plumb, level, and comparison kit under an actual property loan, permitted public extracts, and two defined mine receiving workdays. No fuel accompanied it. Lin would gain a source outside the supplier's private bench and accept a return deadline. Survey instruments could ask questions about ordinary measurements; they could not promise a safe mine before its appropriate people examined it.

shoal_e22_open_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_open_08.text: Rong Sui spoke for the cargo source's current bench invitation, not for every supplier in the port. He Ming brought the consenting travelers' questions, not authority to assign their futures. The pilots' ordinary receiver showed the actual loan case and kept it shut before acceptance. Yue could hear the three opportunities in people she knew, which made the choice harder than reading three neat titles. She would disappoint somebody's hope even if all respected her answer.

shoal_e22_open_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_open_09.text: Rong wanted the plate comparison received on time. He Ming wanted the travelers heard as people whose occupations and bodies differed. The pilots' receiver wanted their tools returned on the proper scope and date after independent observations. Each need was credible. None entitled its advocate to Lin's next season. She asked what her ordinary two paid receiving days would actually involve, then listened for the part each role would leave unavailable.

shoal_e22_open_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_open_10.text: At the mine, Days Four Hundred Forty-Two and Forty-Three would pay five copper each after performed ordinary receiving. Arrival room and meals covered Four Forty through Four Forty-Three. Later work and housing would need actual new terms or her own money. She would enter ordinary mine clearance on Four Forty-Four rather than simultaneously working those receiving days and claiming full attendance elsewhere. The road invitation did not hire her for the entire mine.

shoal_e22_open_11.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_open_11.text: The five travelers had separately confirmed their own thirty-copper road living provision after meeting current port costs through departure. Their settled trade earnings and actual personal arrangements were not part of the association's ninety-two-copper arrival account. One other interested worker declined because the present road costs and leaving time did not suit her household. The group respected that refusal. Choosing a worker journey would help these particular consenting adults, not claim all displaced people now had a road.

shoal_e22_open_12.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_open_12.text: Yue wanted independent questions and also wanted the supplier source's sharper technical access. She liked the idea of traveling with people and knew people could require patience that a closed loan case did not. Her renewed marker qualification did not answer this conflict. It could perform one small local task under its conditions. The decision concerned the next work, company, and property she was actually willing to accept.

shoal_e22_open_13.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_open_13.text: Before the reply deadline, she asked each advocate whether declining this offer would remove her already earned port wages or source rights. It would not. The cargo owner could find another suitable escort, the travelers another accepted helper or arrangement, and the pilots another borrower. Current slots might be lost while they did. Lin could respect those consequences and still choose one finite role rather than promise all three.

shoal_e22_open_14.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_open_14.text: She read the final titles once more. Cargo would bring port-owned plates and supplier-bench access, with no household-interview post. The worker journey would bring consenting adults and their offered accounts, with no supplier equipment. Survey would bring lender-owned instruments and permitted public findings, with a dated return and no authority over workers. She selected the scope whose gains and obligations she wanted to carry into the next town.

shoal_terms_choice.speaker: narrator
shoal_terms_choice.text: Yue chose one accepted road toward the mine. The convoy carried six port-owned signal-plate crates and defined supplier-bench access. The refuge journey served five consenting adults with conditional-on-nothing arrival housing, optional statements, and no supplier kit. The survey carried the pilots' unpowered loan tools and public extracts due back through an authorized receiver. Each paid only two performed mine receiving days. Its unchosen resources and role would remain unavailable.

choices.text: Escort the port's six signal-plate crates to the supplier receiving.
Travel with the five consenting workers toward their chosen new possibilities.
Carry the pilots' survey instruments for independent permitted observations.

shoal_terms_convoy.speaker: narrator
shoal_terms_convoy.text: Yue accepted the cargo scope and Rong took the actual current reply to its owner. He looked pleased before remembering that acceptance was not completion. The six signal-plate crates would remain in the secured gallery until their proper port receiving. Lin had no right to open them privately on the road or use their contents to power a personal task. Her ordinary escort role concerned custody, defined questions, and an actual supplier receiving.

shoal_e22_convoy_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_convoy_02.text: The new fifty-copper convoy account reserved ten for Lin's two performed five-copper mine days, twenty-four for the licensed shared carrier, eight for four arrival days' room and meals, four packing, and four receipt messages. None paid her fifteen road living days; thirty from own money would cover those. The port owner had accepted the source specifically for these six crates. It had not promised wages for a new mine job afterward.

shoal_e22_convoy_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_convoy_03.text: The supplier-bench invitation would be limited to current plate receiving and comparison under its qualified supervisor. It licensed no copy of a private appendix that Lin had never received on this road. Even if her earlier Lark choice had once brought a loan kit, that kit had returned on its actual date. Rong understood why she asked and looked faintly exasperated at having to promise only what his current owner could actually offer.

shoal_e22_convoy_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_convoy_04.text: The travelers' helper place remained unaccepted by her. He Ming would need to seek another suitable arrangement with those five adults, and their current road opportunity could change while he did. Lin did not receive their private interviews or housing role by wishing them well. The pilots retained their instruments without a loan to her. This cargo decision had made one technical source available and left two different kinds of access behind.

shoal_e22_convoy_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_convoy_05.text: Rong introduced the gallery keeper whose employer actually held the crates. The keeper knew their numbering better than he knew Lin's cultivation stage. He asked how she would report a broken seal before the destination. She described the ordinary carrier receiving and named notification scope in the terms. He approved of the answer and asked her to read the exact exception clause because good intentions did not tell a consignee what had happened.

shoal_e22_convoy_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_convoy_06.text: A damaged seal would require the proper carrier and owner receiving, not a secret repair by Lin. Safety concerns could require a stop and appropriate ordinary review. Ownership did not compel her to keep traveling through a condition outside the accepted road terms. The keeper pointed to the actual stop and notice process once, then closed the agreement. He wanted an escort who could use it, not someone who merely admired a neat paragraph.

shoal_e22_convoy_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_convoy_07.text: The six crates held ordinary freight-signal plates suitable for their accepted technical comparison. They were stored outside both affected sheds before the later fire and had stayed in the secured gallery. The keeper showed the permitted outside inventory and actual custody history. They were not an improbable hidden duplicate of lost private tools. Their existence belonged to a separate current port project, one that had also suffered delays without losing this particular stock.

shoal_e22_convoy_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_convoy_08.text: Lin would attend two one-hour unpaid preparation visits before departure under the finite acceptance, then perform the two paid mine receiving days. She agreed because the road's funded carrier and access suited the scope she wanted. Rong could not add open-ended extra port labor afterward. The owner had qualified workers for actual packing and loading under their own pay. Lin's task would not become a heavy carry because a cultivator's name now appeared beside the cargo.

shoal_e22_convoy_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_convoy_09.text: At the first preliminary conversation, the keeper asked whether she wanted a plate displayed on the public board. She refused an unoffered public copy and asked what permitted extract the owner had accepted. The current route identification could be displayed, while particular supplier geometry stayed within its licensed comparison. The difference would let a worker know what shipment she escorted without publishing technical material its owner had never offered.

shoal_e22_convoy_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_convoy_10.text: Rong wanted to explain the bench's advantages. He drew a rough permitted outline and pointed to the contact position their qualified people wanted to compare. Lin could see why the source interested him. A present actual plate would answer sharper questions than a rumor about a device. It would also place her questions inside an owner's purpose and hours. The choice was attractive for that reason and restrictive for the same reason.

shoal_e22_convoy_11.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_convoy_11.text: She asked whether a poor result could be included in a permitted public safety warning. The owner would retain private technical detail, while current safety findings needed their appropriate responsible receiving and disclosure scope. Rong supplied the actual clause instead of promising to publicize every private diagram. Lin would not accept secrecy that required a known current hazard be hidden from the people lawfully responsible for it. The agreement kept that duty distinct from an unlimited copying license.

shoal_e22_convoy_12.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_convoy_12.text: The keeper had a daughter applying for ordinary work at the mine. He asked Lin to deliver a separate family message if its carrier scope allowed. It did not belong in the convoy source or crates. He could book an actual personal message through the proper office. Lin declined to hide it inside property receiving. He nodded, disappointed by the convenience lost and pleased she had not accepted a task whose costs nobody had named.

shoal_e22_convoy_13.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_convoy_13.text: At the gallery doorway, a worker recognized her from the fire stories and asked whether the plates would be protected by qi on the road. She described the ordinary packing, carrier, and actual custody process. Her small marker task was no traveling shield. The worker said he preferred good padding anyway because it did not become tired halfway to an inn. The keeper laughed and went to check the packing material actually ordered.

shoal_e22_convoy_14.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_convoy_14.text: The owner expected a defined supplier comparison at the mine, not a promise that Lin would agree with every result. She would receive sources and ordinary findings within her role. Qualified people would perform whatever technical work the current invitation actually covered. If an examination remained uncertain, its uncertainty could travel in the proper report. A useful escort was not one who made a successful result by calling an inconclusive one success.

shoal_e22_convoy_15.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_convoy_15.text: Lin walked outside with Rong after the current discussion. He asked whether choosing cargo meant she finally preferred suppliers to households. She said it meant she had chosen this role. The port had taught her that people wanted choices to explain more than their actual terms. He admitted he had been hoping for a flattering answer. She said he would need to pay a performer for one. He laughed without taking the joke as a sale.

shoal_e22_convoy_16.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_convoy_16.text: That afternoon the pilots' receiver closed her tentative survey place after the actual refusal. The kit remained available only through a different accepted borrower. Lin held no instruments or independent survey mandate. The five workers continued their own decisions with He Ming's ordinary receiving. A choice could leave other institutions competent enough to seek another path while still remove particular opportunities from Lin's own next town.

shoal_e22_convoy_17.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_convoy_17.text: She updated her own road record to name cargo escort, six port-owned plate crates, and defined supplier receiving. The title did not qualify mine work, command a crew, or grant a private house. Her current stage-six application record remained attached only for the narrow body task it described. Sui could inspect the actual departure arrangement without assuming Lin's cultivation had replaced ordinary travel dates and ownership lines.

shoal_e22_convoy_18.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_convoy_18.text: At home she imagined the mine's supplier room and noticed how much of that imagination came from Rong's enthusiasm. She had not yet stood there. Its actual people might disagree, its bench could be crowded, and its current conditions would need receiving when she arrived. The accepted invitation gave a path into a technical source. It did not give her the result or a picture of every relationship she would find inside.

shoal_e22_convoy_19.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_convoy_19.text: She wrote the two paid dates, Four Hundred Forty-Two and Forty-Three, beside the four funded arrival days. All later housing and work would need separate terms or her own money. The source's ten wage copper stayed future until those receiving days were performed. Lin had accepted a finite task across a real fifteen-day road and had enough own provision to travel it without asking the plate owner to supply meals it had never promised.

shoal_e22_convoy_20.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_convoy_20.text: Rong returned the accepted copy with the owner's actual acknowledgment before the reply window closed. The cargo source was now her selected road, with the current port preparation still to be performed. The other two scopes had not become hidden favors in her pack. Lin folded the copy and went to tell He Ming and the pilots' receiver her answer directly, making the refusal concrete enough that they could plan without waiting for her.

shoal_terms_refuge.speaker: narrator
shoal_terms_refuge.text: Yue accepted the worker-journey scope. He Ming brought the five adults to the ordinary receiving table at their separately offered time. Bai Fen worked with tiles, Yan He baskets, Pei Lu kitchens, Xu Zhen timber, and Jin Shu wool. Their occupations did not become a group job at the mine. Each would decide what actual offers to consider there. Xu's preexisting shoulder restrictions remained part of his ordinary travel arrangements rather than a problem Lin would heal.

shoal_e22_refuge_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_refuge_02.text: The ninety-two-copper source reserved ten for Lin's two performed five-copper receiving days, twenty-four for six road tickets, eight for Lin's four arrival days' board, forty for the five adults' four arrival days, and ten for up to five optional two-copper statements. A statement would be paid only if actually offered and performed. Tickets and housing required no testimony. The source did not contain wages for promised jobs, because no such jobs had been offered.

shoal_e22_refuge_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_refuge_03.text: Each traveler had already settled their current port costs through departure and separately reserved thirty own copper for fifteen road living days at two each. They named their own means within the receiving necessary for booking, without giving the office control of every private purchase. The funded tickets did not feed them on the road. Lin reserved her own thirty too. The actual ordinary living cost belonged to six people whose purses stayed separate.

shoal_e22_refuge_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_refuge_04.text: Bai Fen wanted to see whether a mine town needed her tile skill. She did not want to call the trip a new life before finding an actual place to work. Yan He wanted to examine basket demand before deciding whether the mine suited his actual work. Pei Lu hoped for a kitchen with steadier hours. Xu Zhen wanted lighter timber-related work compatible with current restrictions. Jin Shu wanted to compare wool prices and decide whether the town suited her at all.

shoal_e22_refuge_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_refuge_05.text: He Ming asked whether the title refuge implied they must stay together. They said no, and the receiving terms agreed. It named the source's temporary arrival support, not authority over adult destinations. A consenting traveler could use the ordinary process to change a route or leave the group within their actual means and terms. Lin's helper role would support receiving and communication, not keep people together by overriding their answers.

shoal_e22_refuge_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_refuge_06.text: Rong closed the tentative supplier-bench invitation after Lin declined the cargo role. No plate crates or kit would travel under her custody. The pilots retained their loan instruments too. Her next town would offer fewer technical sources through this road and more ordinary people able to choose which accounts they shared. The loss of bench access felt sharp. She accepted it rather than pretending concern for workers would make a supplier's private room open automatically.

shoal_e22_refuge_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_refuge_07.text: At the table, Pei Lu asked whether she had to tell a sad story to retain her arrival bed. She did not. The four days' ordinary room and meals were funded regardless of optional statements. She could describe a useful current work question, decline altogether, or choose a narrower offered account if the receiving actually suited it. The source's small statement payment was no purchase of all her experience or proof that an interviewer had served her well.

shoal_e22_refuge_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_refuge_08.text: Xu Zhen asked who would lift his baggage. He had arranged a modest load and the carrier's accepted ordinary handling within the ticket scope. Lin was not a substitute for safe loading merely because she cultivated. Xu's current shoulder restrictions stayed visible to appropriate people under his consent. The group would not test him by making him prove endurance in front of strangers. He could refuse an unsuitable physical task without surrendering his place.

shoal_e22_refuge_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_refuge_09.text: Yan He wanted a particular basket kept in his own custody rather than packed with communal belongings. It held his current examples of ordinary basket work, and he did not offer its contents for inspection beyond ordinary carrier requirements. The clerk marked the actual bag on his passenger list. Lin's journey role did not make every traveler's property part of one institutional collection. A group could share a road without sharing a cupboard.

shoal_e22_refuge_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_refuge_10.text: Bai Fen asked about costs after the four funded arrival days. The clerk gave the actual mine receiving dates and ordinary later housing process. No employer or permanent room had been promised. Each traveler would need their own money, a separately accepted opportunity, or a chosen onward road after the arrival term. Bai had planned for that uncertainty and still wanted to go. The clerk did not make her optimism into a guarantee for the others.

shoal_e22_refuge_11.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_refuge_11.text: One interested worker, who had declined the present trip, visited to wish them well. Her household needed her current port work, and thirty road living copper could not be set aside without missing rent. The group did not collect an unaccepted compulsory gift or shame her for staying. She might consider another road later. The present source had five actual consenting adults and could not become support for every person who wanted a different future.

shoal_e22_refuge_12.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_refuge_12.text: Lin accepted two one-hour unpaid preparation visits under this finite arrangement before the paid mine receiving days. The group would use them to confirm actual bookings and offered contact preferences, while each person retained their own pack and choices. It was not an indefinite promise to solve every personal problem. He Ming had other ordinary receiving work and wanted the scope clear enough that travelers would know when to use the staffed office instead.

shoal_e22_refuge_13.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_refuge_13.text: During the preliminary conversation, Jin Shu asked whether a report from the mine might be sent home even if she decided not to stay. The source could receive an optional statement within its actual terms; personal private messages would need their own route and cost. She wanted both possibilities distinguished. An account of wool prices for the association did not automatically contain a letter to a contact, and the recipient had not agreed to be named publicly.

shoal_e22_refuge_14.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_refuge_14.text: The travelers disagreed about the earliest ordinary start each morning. Pei Lu liked dawn because kitchens taught her to work before the crowd. Yan He hated dawn and preferred a longer evening. Their carrier had actual departure hours at its road stops. They could plan personal rest around those limits without turning a preference into a command for everyone. Lin listened long enough to learn that cooperation would not mean an absence of argument.

shoal_e22_refuge_15.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_refuge_15.text: Xu Zhen watched Lin listening and asked whether she regretted declining the instruments. Lin said she wanted the technical source and had chosen this role anyway. Xu liked that answer better than a declaration that people always mattered more than tools. He had earned money with tools for years. The decision concerned a particular accepted journey, where those tools were not available and these particular people had chosen to travel.

shoal_e22_refuge_16.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_refuge_16.text: The port office would not report them all employed when they reached the mine. Their first actual task there was receiving their chosen temporary support and deciding what to offer next. Lin's ten wage copper depended on her two performed receiving days, not on making the adults accept jobs. A helper could succeed at ordinary receiving while a traveler decided the town was wrong for her and chose an actual onward road.

shoal_e22_refuge_17.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_refuge_17.text: He Ming asked them to name which current contact could receive a delay message. Bai chose a fellow tile worker; Yan chose his colleague; Pei named a kitchen colleague; Xu offered a consenting neighbor; Jin supplied a permitted address within its ordinary scope. Each answer would need proper actual receiving, and a changed route would need a real message. Lin could not replace that process with a promise that she would know every household's thoughts.

shoal_e22_refuge_18.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_refuge_18.text: At home Lin considered how the mine might feel without supplier-bench access. She would arrive with people whose questions came from trades and bodies rather than a private plate design. Some might offer her an account; others might want no conversation. The role suited a patience she wanted to practice and a kind of uncertainty she did not always enjoy. She could admit the cost without calling the choice mistaken before the road began.

shoal_e22_refuge_19.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_refuge_19.text: The accepted copy named only five consenting adults besides Lin and their finite supported arrival term. It did not carry a household mandate over anyone left in the port. The source's optional ten statement copper remained reserved future work, not income already received by travelers. Lin kept her own stage-six record separate from their travel permissions. Her body could not consent for theirs, heal Xu's shoulder, or guarantee a safe life after the four funded days.

shoal_e22_refuge_20.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_refuge_20.text: He Ming returned the acknowledged selected scope before the reply window closed. The worker journey was now Lin's accepted road, with actual port preparation still ahead. The cargo and survey sources remained unchosen, carrying no hidden kit or bench privilege for her. She went to thank their advocates and give her refusals plainly, leaving those institutions free to arrange other people instead of waiting for an answer she had already made.

shoal_terms_survey.speaker: narrator
shoal_terms_survey.text: Yue accepted the independent survey scope. The pilots' receiver opened the actual loan case for its preliminary offered view and left every item inside its current custody. A plumb, level, and unpowered comparison kit belonged to the Outer Shoal Pilots' Association. No fuel, spirit stones, private supplier appendix, or body-route diagram accompanied them. Lin would receive the property properly during the next port preparation, not acquire ownership by admiring it today.

shoal_e22_survey_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_survey_02.text: The fifty-copper source reserved ten for Lin's two performed five-copper mine days, twenty-four for shared carrier fare, eight four-day arrival board, four permitted copying, and four return dispatch. Thirty own copper would fund personal road living over the fifteen actual days. The four arrival days did not promise a permanent room. The two receiving days did not promise a mine job. The tools' particular permissions were useful enough to be worth their limits.

shoal_e22_survey_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_survey_03.text: The comparison kit measured ordinary external questions within its suitable scope. Lin would use qualified ordinary sources and local permissions to identify what could actually be observed. She would not pronounce every seam stable or operate a mine machine by holding a plumb. A public extract could make a limited finding available without carrying every private workshop's information. Independent meant a different source of work, not unlimited access to everyone else's.

shoal_e22_survey_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_survey_04.text: The loan's return deadline was Day Five Hundred. It would be met through the lender-authorized licensed carrier receiving at the mine, with the actual case condition and custody receipt. Onward physical travel to the pilots' headquarters remained the carrier's duty and would take its real road time. Lin would not write that the tools had arrived at the harbor merely because an authorized receiver had taken them into proper custody elsewhere.

shoal_e22_survey_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_survey_05.text: The receiver expected the ordinary loan work to finish at the mine in time for authorized return on Four Hundred Ninety-Six. Actual custody, rather than instant arrival in the harbor, would complete Lin's obligation. The proposed date allowed the Five Hundred deadline to be honored without inventing a four-day journey back across a fifteen-day road. The signed clause made that meaning clear before the tools left their cupboard or any later carrier received them.

shoal_e22_survey_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_survey_06.text: Rong closed Lin's tentative supplier-bench invitation after the cargo refusal. The six port-owned crates would travel only under another actual arrangement, without her custody. He Ming would seek a different suitable route with the five consenting adults. Lin held no worker-interview appointment through this survey. She had selected an external measurement source and lost two other kinds of access she had wanted to keep.

shoal_e22_survey_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_survey_07.text: The pilots' receiver asked what she would do if a tool fell outside its observed condition on the road. Lin described the accepted stop, notice, and qualified ordinary assessment process. She would not secretly bend a level straight with qi or treat a damaged line as reliable because a deadline approached. The owner could decide replacement or repair under actual terms. A borrower could be useful by reporting a bad instrument before its figures traveled farther.

shoal_e22_survey_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_survey_08.text: At the preliminary table, she could see a scratch on the level's outer casing. The receiver had already recorded it. They checked its ordinary functional observation separately from its appearance. A scratch could be harmless in one place and meaningful in another. Lin wanted the actual accepted condition recorded so return would not become an argument over a mark that existed before she touched the case.

shoal_e22_survey_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_survey_09.text: One pilot asked whether six pairs would let her survey from above the mine without ordinary access. Lin said she possessed no flight qualification or such method. The instruments belonged in places whose actual holders permitted suitable observation. The pilot grinned and admitted he had been hoping for an easier view. He still wanted the independent comparison and knew it would need the ordinary inconvenience of roads, stairs, and asking people who might decline.

shoal_e22_survey_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_survey_10.text: The source's four copying copper covered only accepted permitted extracts. Private material encountered later would retain its owners' rights unless actually offered. Lin could identify an unanswered question without collecting its source by stealth. The pilots preferred a report they could properly use to a stack of exciting figures whose collection they could not explain. Independence would need a source history as ordinary as the instruments' physical condition.

shoal_e22_survey_11.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_survey_11.text: She accepted two one-hour unpaid preparation visits before departure under the finite survey arrangement, then the two paid mine receiving days. The pilots had their own ordinary packer and carrier arrangements funded within actual scopes. Lin would not become an unpaid full-time survey office while waiting for the road. The receiver named where further requests should go after her offered preparation hours ended. Her yes had a size.

shoal_e22_survey_12.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_survey_12.text: At the table, a young pilot asked why she declined people for instruments. Lin said she had chosen this work and not made a general argument that instruments deserved more care. People would continue their actual journeys under other arrangements if they accepted them. A tool could not tell her what kind of life to choose. It could make certain ordinary measurements possible, which was the opportunity she wanted on this particular road.

shoal_e22_survey_13.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_survey_13.text: The pilot said numbers felt less troublesome than people. The receiver answered that a false number could become a troublesome person standing at the wrong place. They laughed, then discussed an actual old chart whose omitted condition had once confused a boat crew. Lin would retain the current conditions beside any permitted extract. A clean figure was not reliable merely because it looked less emotional than an offered worker's account.

shoal_e22_survey_14.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_survey_14.text: Lin asked whether the pilots wanted a successful mine comparison at any cost. They wanted an honest bounded one. Missing access, changed conditions, and doubtful instrument results could be reported within the proper terms. The source paid her actual receiving days and permitted work, not an exciting conclusion. She found that promise easier to accept after a reassessment in which her own unfinished first attempt had remained part of the final record.

shoal_e22_survey_15.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_survey_15.text: The receiver showed the ordinary carrying case's handhold without letting Lin take custody yet. It was suited to the agreed shared carrier scope, but she would still keep her old shoulder restrictions in its handling. A qualified loader would manage the carrier transfer. Small did not mean weightless, and an owner could not make a borrowed case medically suitable by calling its borrower a cultivator. Lin agreed the actual handling method before leaving the room.

shoal_e22_survey_16.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_survey_16.text: At home she imagined independent questions about the mine's ordinary work paths and measured spaces. She had not been invited into every gallery. Current people could refuse a source, and the instruments could reveal an uncertainty instead of a result. That prospect interested her. It also meant she would lack the sharper supplier geometry available through cargo and the offered household relationships available through the worker journey.

shoal_e22_survey_17.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_survey_17.text: She wrote the actual Five Hundred deadline in her own road notebook beside the authorized custody meaning. The future return was a real obligation, not a decorative date. If the current scope could not fit the condition and travel terms, she would need to stop, notify the owner, and arrange the proper receiving rather than pretend an endless borrowed kit had become personal equipment. Planning its return was part of accepting it.

shoal_e22_survey_18.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_survey_18.text: The selected survey source would fund four arrival days and two receiving days only. All later lodging and mine work would require own money or separately accepted terms. Lin had enough personal provision for the ordinary road and retained a margin afterward. The loan instruments did not become money in her purse or an endorsement from the port for every later ambition. They were property held for a defined task and due back through an actual route.

shoal_e22_survey_19.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_survey_19.text: The acknowledged copy returned before the reply window closed. The pilots had accepted her as the current borrower under the finite source, with proper port receiving still ahead. No unpowered instrument had granted her a larger qi task. Her stage-six record remained the same narrow current qualification. The next town would see an ordinary person with borrowed tools, actual questions, and a body whose limits she had now written plainly.

shoal_e22_survey_20.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_survey_20.text: She went to tell Rong and He Ming her refusal directly. Both wanted their own offers fulfilled and accepted that Lin had chosen another. They could seek different suitable people, and current opportunities might change in the meantime. Lin carried the selected loan terms back to her room without a private bench invitation or a worker-group mandate hidden between its pages. Her road had gained a real independent source and left real alternatives behind.

shoal_e22_terms_rejoin_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_terms_rejoin_01.text: The actual chosen reply was received before the current deadline. Lin's next road now had a finite source, specific people or property, and work that would be paid only after it occurred. The other proposed scopes retained their own owners and decisions. She did not carry their unchosen permissions by goodwill. At the public desk, Han removed the tentative lines that no longer described her arrangement and entered the one actually accepted.

shoal_e22_terms_rejoin_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_terms_rejoin_02.text: Sui checked the selected road's ordinary departure plan against the current application record. Fifteen travel days and the arrival receiving dates fit without putting Lin in two towns at once. The captain retained the current small-task and shoulder limits. She did not examine the role as proof that the port had healed everything it had hurt. The plan was suitable work for a particular traveler with actual money, obligations, and boundaries.

shoal_e22_terms_rejoin_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_terms_rejoin_03.text: Over the next few days, Lin arranged her personal pack and current room payment through departure. Two short preparation visits under the chosen scope remained ahead. The funded mine wage stayed future. She had accepted useful work and would need to perform it, while any later mine course or job remained undecided. The harbor's ordinary lane seemed familiar enough that leaving would be difficult, and open enough that staying forever had never been its only possible ending.

shoal_e22_terms_rejoin_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_terms_rejoin_04.text: On Day Four Hundred Fourteen, she set her own pack on the low table and checked what she intended to carry. Clothes, a cup, personal notes, and current provisions belonged to her. The chosen role's property or travelers would require their separate receiving next week. She removed an unnecessary heavy object she had kept from habit. Leaving it with a consenting keeper under actual terms made more sense than proving her shoulder could tolerate it.

shoal_e22_terms_rejoin_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e22_terms_rejoin_05.text: At the window she could hear a worker practicing the refrain from Song's earlier performance. The singer missed one familiar turn and tried again. Yue smiled without judging the whole performance from that moment. Her own road was likewise something she had accepted before knowing every difficulty it would contain. She closed the pack, leaving its role-specific space empty until proper receiving, and went to the current clerk for the first preparation appointment.
